source.title: What Makes Countries Rich
source.summary: The production function, total factor productivity, the Islamic golden age, and why Muslim-majority countries are poorer today.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: Why does a worker in Germany produce ten times more per hour than a worker in Bangladesh? It's not effort. It's capital, technology, and institutions. This episode introduces the production function, explains total factor productivity, and then turns to a puzzle: the Islamic world was the global productivity leader for five centuries. Baghdad, Cordoba, and Cairo were centers of innovation in agriculture, manufacturing, and finance. What drove that? And what happened? The decline wasn't just colonialism. Internal institutional failures, loss of intellectual dynamism, and resistance to new technologies all played a role. Today, Muslim-majority countries are disproportionately in the lower-middle and low-income categories. The honest diagnosis: low TFP, weak institutions, underinvestment in human capital. This series explores whether Islamic economic principles, properly understood, could address these structural problems.
